summary: Thermalito spreads across 12.8 square miles of flat Sacramento Valley floor just south of Oroville, which means the density sits at a remarkably low 519 people per square mile — a figure more consistent with unincorporated ranchette country than a named community, and one that explains why so much of the landscape reads as open fields, orchards, and wide-set residential lots rather than anything resembling a traditional town grid. The nearby Oroville Dam and Lake Oroville — California's second-largest reservoir — anchor the area's identity and provide reservoir recreation within a short drive, while the Thermalito Afterbay and Forebay immediately adjacent offer fishing, walking paths, and surprisingly expansive water views against the backdrop of the Sierra Nevada foothills to the east. At a median home value of $257,400 against a median household income of $53,814, the price-to-income ratio lands around 4.8 — genuinely affordable by California standards, though a 17.2% poverty rate signals that the local economy, driven largely by agriculture, public-sector work, and Oroville-area services, doesn't generate abundant high-wage employment. Summers average 77°F highs with over nine hours of daily sunshine, meaning heat is a defining feature from June through September. Thermalito is the kind of place where affordability and open space come packaged with geographic isolation from major job centers — Chico is roughly 25 miles north, Sacramento about 75 miles south — making it functionally a community where housing costs reward those who've already solved the employment question.
